body:
Summary only - this document is not intended to be used without reference to the Financial Services Rule Book, nor can the Isle of Man Financial Services Authority accept responsibility for its accuracy. It remains the user's responsibility to review the source legislation and ensure compliance with the Rule Book requirements.

This table sets out the obligations in the Financial Services Rule Book 2016 for licenceholders under the Financial Services Act 2008 to maintain policies.

body: Rule 6.31 (Vulnerable clients) - responsibility: A licenceholder; applies to: Class 2; comment: Establish and implement.

6.55 - Valuation of investments
body: Rule 6.55 (Valuation of investments) - responsibility: A licenceholder; applies to: Class 3 (except activities in subclasses 11 or 12); comment: Changes to valuation methods must be agreed by the governing body.

8.6 - Risk management
body: Rule 8.6 (Risk management) - responsibility: Responsible officers; applies to: Classes 1 - 8 (except Class 8(1), 8(2)(b), or 8(3)); comment: Annual review required. See also 8.33 for Class 1 licenceholders.

chunk_id: Financial Services Rule Book 2016 - Rules relating to policies, Financial Services Rule Book 2016 - Rules relating to policies, 8.36 - Credit risk policy - 8b4e113b6f40f2ca
document: Financial Services Rule Book 2016 - Rules relating to policies
headers: Financial Services Rule Book 2016 - Rules relating to policies
8.36 - Credit risk policy
body: Rule 8.36 (Credit risk policy) - responsibility: A licenceholder by its directors; applies to: Class 1 incorporated in IOM; comment: Annual review required under 8.36 and notification to the Authority, within 4 months after the end of its financial year, that during the financial year the directors reviewed and approved the policy and were satisfied that it was up to date and appropriate under 8.47 [Footnote: The Authority's Consent and Notification Summary Table provides further information regarding the various types of events which licenceholders are required to inform the Authority of, either on a notification basis, or prior consent before an action can proceed basis.].
